_comment: The Review-PRs prompt model: depth levels + the scope/action text blocks that the wizard assembles into the agent prompt. Verbatim from ReviewWizard.swift. The assembly order/conditions live as a tiny glue layer in each front-end.

depths.title: Quick static pass
depths.blurb: Read each diff, flag obvious issues. Nothing run.
depths.fragment: Read the review diff and its affected callers for visible regressions or failures of the stated change. This is a quick static pass. Report only consequences the code establishes.

depths.title: Focused review
depths.blurb: Check the changed behavior and verify credible findings in one pass.
depths.fragment: Make one focused pass over the review diff and affected callers. Check the intended behavior and plausible failure paths. Use a targeted test or the real entry point when a result depends on runtime behavior. Finish once you have checked the change and verified your findings.
depths.onBranch: Fix the real findings directly on the PR's branch.

depths.title: Deep · hard repro
depths.blurb: Moves + absence pass; concrete repro before & after every fix.
depths.fragment: For each PR, dispatch swarms of agents across the review moves — claims vs code (every comment, docstring, description, error message, type, test name and README line the change touches or silently falsifies still tells the truth about the code), nearest twin (each changed rule, constant, guard, mapping or message agrees with whatever does the same job elsewhere: the other platform, the other call site, the other arm of the same branch), non-happy paths (errors, timeouts, cancellation, partial success and missing input: what the caller is told, what state is left behind, and above all whether anything reports success for work it did not do), inputs (empty, non-finite, boundary, misspelled or extra keys, alternate spellings, and shapes only one platform produces, including the message each one gets), reachability both ways (whether each branch or guard can actually fire or is shadowed by an earlier check, and whether its value reaches the consumer it was written for), and what outlives the call (processes, temp files, caches, device state, two callers racing one file, and every timeout on the path summed against the budget the code claims) — plus the absence pass, which finds what is missing by comparing against a reference: a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry (spawn/reap, open/close, write/delete, set/reset), and, when coverage of the central behavior is in doubt, a targeted mutation that reverts that behavior. For every suspected HIGH / MEDIUM issue, build a concrete, hard reproduction that proves it real BEFORE touching anything.
depths.onBranch: For each confirmed issue, fix it directly on the PR's branch and re-run the same reproduction to confirm the fix lands.

depths.title: Full E2E · max
depths.blurb: Run the affected workflows end to end and reproduce findings.
depths.fragment: Maximum rigor. For each PR: run it END-TO-END through its real entry point and confirm observable behaviour — not just that it compiles. Dispatch swarms across the review moves — claims vs code (every comment, docstring, description, error message, type, test name and README line the change touches or silently falsifies still tells the truth about the code), nearest twin (each changed rule, constant, guard, mapping or message agrees with whatever does the same job elsewhere: the other platform, the other call site, the other arm of the same branch), non-happy paths (errors, timeouts, cancellation, partial success and missing input: what the caller is told, what state is left behind, and above all whether anything reports success for work it did not do), inputs (empty, non-finite, boundary, misspelled or extra keys, alternate spellings, and shapes only one platform produces, including the message each one gets), reachability both ways (whether each branch or guard can actually fire or is shadowed by an earlier check, and whether its value reaches the consumer it was written for), and what outlives the call (processes, temp files, caches, device state, two callers racing one file, and every timeout on the path summed against the budget the code claims) — plus the absence pass, which finds what is missing by comparing against a reference: a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry (spawn/reap, open/close, write/delete, set/reset), and, when coverage of the central behavior is in doubt, a targeted mutation that reverts that behavior; every HIGH / MEDIUM finding gets a concrete hard reproduction that proves it real.
depths.onBranch: Fix every confirmed finding directly on the PR's branch, with the SAME reproduction re-run after each fix to prove it lands.

scope.single: Review PR #{pr} in {owner}/{repo}. Use the `gh` CLI to fetch it.
scope.multi: Go through {scope} in {owner}/{repo}. Use the `gh` CLI to enumerate them.

_specificComment: A specific PR may be mine OR someone else's, and that decides whether the agent may touch the branch — so the prompt is branched on the polled author. CASE A = mine (fix it); CASE B = theirs (review only, hands off). The wizard only injects each case's action sub-blocks when its toggle is on.

specific.determineAuthor: Before doing anything else, fetch this PR and find out WHO AUTHORED IT: `gh pr view {pr} --repo {owner}/{repo} --json author,isDraft,headRefName`. Everything below depends on the answer — handle the PR as exactly ONE of the two cases that follow, never both.
specific.mineOnly: This PR is MINE (@{me}) — treat it as my own work: fix what you find directly on its branch and push. You have full authority over it.
specific.reviewerFindingsFirst: FIRST AND FOREMOST, resolve every reviewer finding already on this PR before doing anything else. Fetch every review comment/thread others left (`gh pr view {pr} --repo {owner}/{repo} --json reviews,comments` plus `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments`), and for EACH one: screen it (read the exact code it points at), verify whether it is a real issue by building a concrete reproduction, then either FIX it on the branch and re-run the reproduction to confirm the fix lands, or — if it is genuinely a non-issue — dismiss it with a short technical reason. Respond on every thread ("Fixed in <commit_hash>" with the real hash when fixed, or the reasoning when dismissed) and never mark a thread resolved without a reply. Only once every existing reviewer finding is addressed do you move on to your own review below.
specific.theirsOnly: This PR is SOMEONE ELSE'S — they requested my review (@{me} is not the author). This is strictly look-don't-touch: your ONE deliverable is the code review itself, never a change to their branch.
specific.mineHeader: ▸ CASE A — @{me} authored this PR (it's MINE). Treat it like my own work: fix what you find directly on its branch. Do everything in this case:
specific.otherHeader: ▸ CASE B — someone OTHER than @{me} authored this PR (it's THEIRS). This is strictly look-don't-touch — your only deliverable is the review. Do everything in this case instead:
specific.otherNoMarkReady: Do NOT mark this PR ready for review and do NOT change its draft/ready state in any way — it isn't yours to advance; only its author decides that.

blocks.premise:
JUDGE THE PREMISE, NOT ONLY THE DIFF. A PR can be flawless line by line and still be the wrong change, so before the technical review, and with the same rigor, answer three questions for each PR. (1) WHAT IS IT FOR: read its title, description, commits and every issue or thread it links, and state in one sentence the problem it sets out to solve. (2) WHAT DOES IT ASSUME: name the diagnosis and every assumption the approach rests on (what causes the problem, who calls this code, what the platform or a dependency guarantees, which case "cannot happen") and check each against the code yourself. The PR's own account of the cause is a claim to verify, never a fact to build on: trace the reported symptom down to where it originates. (3) IS THIS THE RIGHT FIX: does the change remove that cause, or only stop the symptom from showing? Suspect the second whenever the diff sits away from where the fault originates: a guard, a retry, a sleep or a longer timeout, a special case for the one reported input, a swallowed error, a test loosened until it passes, a cleanup after the fact. Ask what the same cause still breaks with this PR merged (another caller, the other platform, the next input of the same shape), and whether the repo already has a mechanism for this that the PR works around or duplicates. Judge the PR as a whole, even when the technical review covers only part of it.

A PR whose premise fails is NOT clean, however well its diff is built: it is never marked ready, approved, or reported to me as clean. A wrong diagnosis, a false assumption, or a workaround for a cause this repo could fix where it originates is an in-scope behavioral finding like any other, handled the way this run handles every finding, and it is at least MEDIUM, never a LOW or a nitpick, and Blocking on someone else's PR: the problem the PR claims to solve is still there. It takes the same proof as any finding: the real cause named at file:line, plus a concrete demonstration - a case that still fails with the PR applied, the assumption shown false, or the problem gone once the cause is fixed and the workaround removed. Where it is posted, anchor it on the hunk that embodies the approach, and state the real cause and what it still breaks. Its thread closes only once the cause is gone or a reply shows the premise held after all, whatever the thread rules say about an original trigger or a deferral. If no change to the diff can repair it (the problem does not exist, or the real fix is a decision that is not yours to make), say so at the top of your summary instead of forcing a fix. It is still posted wherever findings are posted, but it keeps no swarm loop or run going. A workaround is the right call only when the cause is out of this repo's reach (a dependency, the OS, someone else's service), and then the code has to say so where the workaround lives. An approach you would merely have designed differently, with no case it gets wrong, is a preference: drop it on sight. A failed premise never cuts the technical review short, and your summary to me carries one line per PR: what it is for and whether its premise held.

Beyond a failed premise, a finding must show either a reachable regression against the merge base of the PR’s target branch or a supported case where the submitted head fails a behavior the change explicitly promises. Give the trigger, the expected or base result, the head result and the changed line responsible. Compare the same input on both revisions when the baseline is uncertain. A partial fix can satisfy its stated scope when it removes the cause for the cases it covers. An adjacent defect already present on the base, a preferred design and wording without a behavioral consequence do not qualify. Keep incidental pre-existing defects in the private summary only. Open a follow-up issue only when the operator explicitly asks.
blocks.bar: Verify findings at the selected depth. Spend runtime verification on credible behavioral consequences and rerun the original reproduction before reporting a fix. Size any swarm to the work, with at most eight agents running at once. When a subagent's summary is spilled to a file, open it at the EXACT path that delegation handed back and never by globbing or listing the summary cache: several reviews run at once on this machine against one shared agent home, and those filenames carry a task index and a timestamp but nothing that names their owner, so a pattern match quietly returns a sibling review's findings for a different PR.
blocks.reviewOnly: These PRs are SOMEONE ELSE'S — not your code to change. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES may you commit, push, or otherwise modify their branch: ABSOLUTELY DO NOT touch their branch in any way. Your one and only deliverable is the code review itself.
blocks.incrementalReviewRange: On a first review use the merge-base-to-head diff. On re-review find the most recent submitted, non-dismissed review bearing the Diplomat tag from this account on this PR and its reviewed commit. If that commit is an ancestor of the current head and the PR still targets the same branch, review only the intervening PR changes, their affected callers and unresolved findings. Exclude changes brought in solely from the target branch. On the same head check outstanding threads only. If the reviewed commit is unavailable, history was rewritten, or the target changed, use the full current PR diff. Apply the chosen depth within that range.
blocks.markReady: If a PR turns out perfectly clean — no issues, regressions or bad practices left at ANY level — mark it ready for review and report its number to me. This bar is stricter than the swarm loop's: a pass that stopped because only LOW findings were left is clean enough to stop iterating, but a PR still carrying LOW findings is NOT perfectly clean and does not get marked ready. List every PR you cleared at the end.
blocks.reviewLifecycle: Anything you post on someone else's PR goes in ONE formal GitHub review, built through GitHub's review lifecycle: open it pending, put every comment inside it, then submit it. Never post on the PR through a top-level comment, nor through the standalone `pulls/<number>/comments` endpoint, which publishes every comment as a separate review of its own. (0) CHECK, first, before any review work: list the PR's reviews (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews`) and read the comments of any PENDING one of mine (`.../reviews/<id>/comments`). If one of them does not open with the `\[[Diplomat](` attribution tag (whatever model name follows it), that review is my own draft from the browser: stop right there — post nothing, and say so in your summary. One whose comments all carry the tag, or that has none, was left by an earlier run: you reuse or replace it at (1), and if you end without opening a review, delete it. (1) OPEN, only once your findings are final, right before you fill it: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews -f commit_id=<head sha>` with NO `event` field leaves the review PENDING, visible to nobody but me. GitHub allows one pending review per person per PR, so if that call is refused because one already exists, list the PR's reviews and read the PENDING one's comments. If it has no comments, or every comment opens with the attribution tag, it is yours — opened earlier in this run, or left by an earlier one. If its `commit_id` is the PR's current head, keep using it, after deleting any of its comments this run is not to post; otherwise delete it (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`) and open a fresh one. Otherwise it is my own draft, begun while you worked: stop as in (0). (2) FILL: add each comment anchored to its exact line(s) with the GraphQL `addPullRequestReviewThread` mutation (`pullRequestReviewId` = the pending review's `node_id`; `path`, `line`, `side`, plus `startLine` for a range), and each reply on an existing thread with `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply` carrying the same `pullRequestReviewId`, so it lands inside this review too. (3) SUBMIT, once, after the last comment is in — and right before it, list the pending review's comments again: one that does not open with the attribution tag is mine, added from the browser, so leave the review unsubmitted and stop as in (0). Otherwise: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>/events -f event=COMMENT -f body=<what you checked, the result, and any optional coverage note allowed below>` — COMMENT unless a verdict instruction below explicitly tells you to APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES; such a verdict is this same submission's event, never a second review. Never end your turn with the review still PENDING: its comments reach no one until it is submitted. If you end with no inline comment, thread reply or optional body note to post and no instruction below to submit a review anyway, delete it instead (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`). Neither rule touches a draft of mine: after a stop, never submit, fill, or delete it.
blocks.leaveReviews:
Post your findings in that review. Put each distinct, verified behavioral finding on its changed line and explain the trigger and impact. Leave the choice of fix to the author. Label it Blocking when the consequence warrants holding the merge, for example when the change disables an existing workflow entirely on a supported runtime. Label smaller verified defects Non-blocking. Read existing threads from every reviewer first, including resolved threads. Keep one thread per defect. For an unresolved thread, retry the original trigger on the current head. Once that trigger passes, the finding is fixed. Never extend its acceptance criteria with a different input or mutant. A new defect in the intervening changes must independently pass the scope test. Reply on the original thread only when a claimed fix still fails its original trigger or you have new evidence relevant to the discussion. Respect a reasoned deferral. Leave resolved threads alone.

A surviving mutant alone shows a coverage gap. When reverting the PR’s central behavior leaves its tests green, you may include one short Optional coverage note in the review body. Combine related gaps there. A coverage note earns no inline thread, holds up no verdict and requires no further pass. Drop incidental test gaps.
blocks.noReviews: Do NOT post your findings on the PR — no inline comments, no thread replies, no top-level comments; report them to me in your summary instead. This outranks every other line here that puts findings in the review or says to post them. Only an instruction below that explicitly tells you to submit a review may post anything.
blocks.reply: For review threads that OTHERS have left on these PRs: address each one, and never mark a thread resolved without first replying "Fixed in <commit_hash>" with the real commit hash.
blocks.noVerdict: Do NOT submit an APPROVE or a REQUEST-CHANGES verdict — the final approve / changes-requested call is mine. Any review you submit on this PR uses the neutral COMMENT event, never APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES. If the PR comes back clean with no behavioral finding or optional coverage note to post, don't post an LGTM — delete any pending review you opened, and just tell me in your summary that PR #{pr} looks clean and is ready for my approval.
blocks.softApprove: Do NOT submit an APPROVE or a REQUEST-CHANGES verdict. When there are no in-scope behavioral findings, submit a COMMENT review with a short body saying what you actually checked and thanking the author (“Thank you for contributing”). Include an optional coverage note only when posting findings is enabled. This is a COMMENT review carrying that body ONLY, never as a top-level issue comment.
blocks.trailer: Keep dispatching swarms until every PR you go through comes back clean — where CLEAN means a pass that surfaced no HIGH and no MEDIUM finding. A pass whose findings are all LOW (or nitpicks) COUNTS AS CLEAN: drop the nitpicks and stop iterating on that PR. Only a HIGH or a MEDIUM keeps the loop alive.
blocks.lowsMine: On my own PR, a finding is never posted — not as an inline comment, a review, or a top-level comment — it is FIXED on the branch. This includes LOW findings that meet the review scope. Re-run their checks after fixing them. Treat every finding an earlier Diplomat run already posted on the PR under my own login (a comment opening with the Diplomat tag) exactly like a reviewer's: fix it or dismiss it with a reason, reply "Fixed in <commit_hash>" or the reason on its thread, then resolve that thread. Finish only with ZERO pending findings on the PR: none left unfixed, and no finding thread left without a reply.
blocks.noAttribution: No AI attribution anywhere in git/GitHub — commits authored as me, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with" taglines.
blocks.diplomatTag: Diplomat attribution tag — a REQUIRED exception to the no-attribution rule, for GitHub commentary only: every comment, inline review comment, review body, and review-thread reply you post as part of this task must begin with the exact prefix `\[[Diplomat](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat){model}\]: `, copied character for character — the `\[` and `\]` are literal brackets, only the word Diplomat is a Markdown link (to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat), anything after that link is plain text, and a colon and a space close it — followed by the text you would otherwise have written, so it renders as "[Diplomat{model}]: <your text>". This is the ONE sanctioned attribution; it applies to posted comment/review text ONLY and never changes commit messages, commit authorship, or the no-Co-Authored-By / no-"Generated with" git rules, which remain in force.
blocks.finalPass: Submit the verdict in the same formal review. Request changes only for a verified in-scope blocker that still applies at the reviewed head. If the scoped checks pass with only non-blocking findings or an optional coverage note, still APPROVE. For a clean result, confirm that previously reported blockers are addressed and approve. Follow the same posting and thread rules for all verdicts.
blocks.finalVerification: Use the full merge-base-to-head diff, even when this head was reviewed before. Before submitting the verdict, run one final FULL E2E pass on the built binaries for the workflows affected by that diff. Use additional agents where the work warrants it.
